title: Basic TCP connect scan
description: Default SYN scan against the top 1000 most common TCP ports (requires no special privileges when run as an ordinary user, falls back to connect scan).
output:
Not shown: 997 closed ports
PORT   STATE SERVICE
22/tcp open  ssh
notes: Always confirm you are authorized to scan the target before running any scan.

title: Scan specific ports
description: Restrict the scan to a specific comma-separated list of ports.
notes: -p- scans all 65535 TCP ports; -p1-1024 scans a range.

title: Scan all 65535 ports
description: Scan every TCP port instead of just the default top-1000.
notes: Slow on large ranges — combine with -T4 and consider --min-rate to speed it up.

title: Service/version detection
description: Probe open ports to determine the service name and version running on them.
notes: --version-intensity 0-9 trades scan speed against probe thoroughness.

title: OS detection
description: Attempt to fingerprint the target's operating system from TCP/IP stack behavior.
notes: Requires at least one open and one closed port for reliable results; needs root/administrator privileges.

title: Aggressive scan
description: Enables OS detection, version detection, script scanning, and traceroute in one flag.
notes: Very noisy on the wire and easily flagged by IDS — use in authorized assessments only.

title: SYN stealth scan
description: Half-open TCP scan that never completes the 3-way handshake, historically 'stealthier' and faster than a full connect.
notes: Requires raw-socket privileges (root/administrator).

title: UDP scan
description: Scan UDP ports, which have no handshake and are inherently slower/less reliable to scan than TCP.
notes: UDP scans are much slower — narrow the port list rather than scanning all 65535 UDP ports.

title: TCP connect scan
description: Full TCP three-way-handshake scan; the fallback scan type for unprivileged users.
notes: More detectable than -sS since it completes full connections that get logged by the target.

title: FIN scan
description: Stealth scan sending only a FIN flag; some stateless firewalls fail to block it since no SYN is sent.
notes: Doesn't work reliably against modern Windows TCP/IP stacks, which ignore the FIN probe.

title: Null scan
description: Sends TCP packets with no flags set at all, another firewall/IDS-evasion technique.
notes: Like -sF/-sX, relies on RFC 793 behavior that not all stacks correctly implement.

title: Xmas scan
description: Sends packets with the FIN, PSH and URG flags set (lit up like a Christmas tree).
notes: Purely for evasion against older/misconfigured stateless filters; unreliable against modern hosts.

title: Ping scan (host discovery only)
description: Discover live hosts on a subnet without port-scanning them.
output:
Nmap scan report for 10.0.0.5
Host is up (0.002s latency).
notes: Fast first step before running a detailed scan against only the hosts that responded.

title: Skip host discovery
description: Treat every target as online and skip the initial ping check — needed when ICMP is blocked.
notes: Without -Pn, Nmap may report a live but ICMP-filtered host as 'down' and skip it entirely.

title: Default script scan
description: Run Nmap's default set of non-intrusive NSE scripts against detected services.
notes: -sC is shorthand for --script=default.

title: Run a specific NSE script
description: Run a named Nmap Scripting Engine script (or category/wildcard) against the target.
notes: --script=vuln runs the whole vulnerability-detection script category — expect a long runtime.

title: Vulnerability scan category
description: Run the 'vuln' category of NSE scripts, which check for numerous known CVEs/misconfigurations.
notes: Can be intrusive; some scripts in this category may crash fragile services — test in a lab first.

title: Timing template
description: Set a timing template from 0 (paranoid) to 5 (insane) controlling scan speed vs stealth.
notes: T3 is the default; T4 is commonly used on reliable local networks for a good speed/accuracy balance.

title: Output to file (normal)
description: Save scan results in normal human-readable format to a file.
notes: -oA basename writes normal, XML and grepable formats simultaneously in one run.

title: Output to XML
description: Save scan results in XML, suitable for parsing by other tools (e.g. to feed into a report generator).
notes: xsltproc can convert Nmap's XML output into an HTML report using the bundled stylesheet.

title: Grepable output
description: Save results in a legacy line-per-host format that's easy to grep/awk.
notes: Officially deprecated by the Nmap project but still widely used in quick shell pipelines.

title: Firewall/IDS evasion — fragmentation
description: Split probe packets into smaller fragments to slip past some simple packet-filtering firewalls/IDS.
notes: -ff fragments even more aggressively (8-byte fragments); modern stateful firewalls reassemble anyway.

title: Decoy scan
description: Make the scan appear to originate from multiple spoofed decoy IPs alongside the real one.
notes: 'ME' controls the position of your real IP among the decoys in the sequence.

title: Spoof source port
description: Send probes from a specific source port, e.g. 53, to slip past port-based firewall rules.
notes: Some older/misconfigured firewalls implicitly trust traffic sourced from port 53 (DNS).

title: Set min packet rate
description: Force Nmap to send at least N packets per second, dramatically speeding up large scans.
notes: Too aggressive a rate can trigger IDS alerts or overwhelm fragile network gear — tune for the environment.

title: Exclude hosts
description: Exclude specific hosts or ranges from a broader scan.
notes: Useful for skipping known-fragile devices (printers, IoT) during a subnet-wide scan.

title: Read targets from file
description: Read the list of scan targets from a text file, one host/range per line.
notes: Combine with --excludefile to subtract an out-of-scope list from the same input.

title: Traceroute
description: Trace the network path to the target as part of the scan.
notes: Included automatically by -A; standalone useful when you don't need the rest of an aggressive scan.

title: Banner grabbing script
description: Grab service banners on open ports to help identify software/version.
notes: Banners are self-reported by the service and can be altered/faked, so verify independently.

title: SMB enumeration script
description: Enumerate SMB shares exposed by a Windows/Samba host.
notes: Pair with smb-os-discovery and smb-enum-users for a fuller Windows host profile.

title: HTTP title grab
description: Fetch and display the <title> of the web page served on detected HTTP ports.
notes: A fast way to fingerprint what's running across a whole subnet of web servers.

title: Compare scan results
description: Compare two Nmap XML scan results to highlight what changed between them (new/closed ports, new hosts).
notes: Bundled with Nmap; excellent for periodic attack-surface drift monitoring.
